text:
leo_sales: Cerulean (fintech) wants Redwood Private behind their perimeter NGFW. Requirements: preserve client src IP for SIEM correlation, small stable set of egress IPs for a 30-day eval, and webhooks must show original client IPs. Can we sketch options + quick runbook they can hand to netops?

ania_se: Two main patterns + tradeoffs: 
- Routed peering / TGW w/ BGP: preserves original source IP end-to-end (no SNAT), so SIEM/webhook source checks work natively. More network work (BGP/route exchange) and requires return-path validation to avoid asymmetry.
- Interface PrivateLink (ENI): fast to provision but customer traffic gets SNATed to the interface ENI IP; original client IP is not visible to backend. You can mitigate with an internal forward proxy that injects X-Forwarded-For, but that adds infra on the customer side.

mark_netops: A few operational caveats: 
- PrivateLink ENIs are per-AZ; callbacks may come from different ENI IPs depending on AZ failover. If customer needs a single allowlist CIDR, reserved EIPs on our egress gateway are better.
- We can provide an ephemeral sticky NAT set (3-5 IPs) for POCs. Its sticky per-connection but not a /24. Reserve request triggers an infra "egress isolation" surcharge for the POC.
- mTLS: if their NGFW performs TLS-inspect, client certs are terminated and you lose mTLS validation. For client-cert pinning, routed peering passthrough is recommended.

sylvia_cs: Security-questionnaire friendly blurb they can paste: 
"Redwood Private supports routed peering (recommended for preservation of original client source IP and for mTLS passthrough) and interface-based PrivateLink (interface endpoints). PrivateLink interface endpoints perform NAT to the endpoint ENI IP and therefore do not preserve original client IPs; to preserve client identity in that topology the customer must run a forward proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For. Temporary static egress IPs can be allocated for evaluation POCs; a small infrastructure surcharge applies for exclusive egress allocations."

leo_sales: Great. Can we get a minimal firewall/DNS checklist and a tiny runbook for their netops? Keep it one page.

ania_se: Runbook snippet (copy-paste):
```
Topology options: Peering/TGW (preserve src IP) OR PrivateLink (quick, NATs src IP)
If Peering/TGW:
  - Establish TGW or VPC peering attachment with Redwood
  - Exchange routes via BGP (our ASN) or static routes; verify symmetric return path
  - Request reserved POC egress IPs via support ticket -> update NGFW outbound allowlist to those IPs (TCP/443)
If PrivateLink:
  - Create Interface Endpoint in chosen subnets (one per AZ)
  - Allow inbound from endpoint ENI CIDRs to application subnets for callbacks/webhooks
Common firewall/DNS preflight:
  - Allow outbound TCP/443 to RESERVED_EIP_LIST (we will provide)
  - Allow UDP/123 to NTP if host time validation is required
  - Ensure private DNS resolves redwood.private.<region> -> peering IP or endpoint DNS name
TLS-inspect notes:
  - If NGFW performs TLS-inspect, bypass Redwood hostnames for flows requiring client certs/mTLS OR deploy an internal passthrough proxy that preserves client certs and forwards X-Forwarded-For.
```

mark_netops: Additional notes for their SIEM/webhook owners: 
- If you use PrivateLink and cannot run a proxy, ask security to accept the endpoint ENI CIDRs as webhook sources or use a small reserved EIP set so callbacks come from stable IPs.
- Healthchecks: if internal health probes originate from multiple AZs make sure webhook auth rules accept those AZ-specific ENI IPs or the reserved EIP set.

ticket-bot: Created ticket RWD-11022: "Cerulean POC - reserve sticky egress IPs & peering guidance". ETA 48 business hours. Owner: ania_se. Billing tag: POC egress isolation surcharge.

leo_sales: Thanks all. I'll send the runbook + security blurb to the customer and ask them to pick topology. Sylvia, please attach ticket to the handoff calendar invite and schedule 30m with their netsec + ops.

sylvia_cs: Invite sent for Thurs 3pm PT, attached runbook + security blurb + ticket link.

leo_sales: Awesome, closing this thread. Will update once they pick peering vs endpoint. :thumbsup:
